🌌 Ethics & Safety

Artificial general intelligence (AGI)

In simple words

A possible future AI that could learn almost any mental task a human can; it doesn't exist yet.

A possible future AI that could learn and do almost any mental task a human can. It doesn't exist yet, and experts disagree about whether and when it will.

Example. Today's AI is mostly “narrow”: a chess program can't drive a car. An AGI could switch between very different tasks, just as people do.

Related words

  • Artificial intelligence (AI)Computer systems that can do tasks that usually need human intelligence.
  • Turing testAlan Turing's 1950 test: a machine passes if people chatting with it in text can't reliably tell it from a human.
  • AI alignmentMaking sure an AI tries to do what people really intend and value, not just what they literally said.
